citeAs: Tjong Kim Sang, Erik F., and Fien De Meulder. (2003). Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition. CoNLL-2003.
creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang, Fien De Meulder (University of Antwerp)
description: A named entity recognition dataset for English and German consisting of training, development, test, and large unannotated files. The annotated files label four entity types—PER, ORG, LOC, and MISC—using the IOB scheme, with one word per line plus part-of-speech, chunk, and named entity tags.
name: CoNLL-2003 named entity data
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of the English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly MUC conventions were followed, with an additional MISC category for names not belonging to PER, ORG, or LOC.
rai:dataCollection: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus and the German data from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically German newspaper text from Frankfurter Rundschau. For each language, the dataset includes training, development, test, and large unannotated files.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data consists of Reuters news stories for English and German newspaper articles from Frankfurter Rundschau in the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus. The dataset also includes large files of unannotated raw text containing 17 million English tokens and 14 million German tokens.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English articles are from August 1996 to December 1996, with unannotated raw data from September 1996. German annotated articles are from one week at the end of August 1992, with raw data from September to December 1992.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The data was split into training, development, test, and large unannotated files for each language. The development/test split was chosen to avoid systems being tuned to the test data.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Before release, the raw text was linguistically preprocessed with language-specific tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, and chunking. English was tagged and chunked with the memory-based MBT tagger, while German was lemmatized, tagged, and chunked with TreeTagger.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for developing and evaluating language-independent named entity recognition systems, including systems that use machine learning and optionally exploit gazetteers or unannotated data.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Language-specific tokenizers, the memory-based MBT tagger for English, and TreeTagger for German were used in preprocessing prior to annotation release.
